newsitem.title: BELGIUM: German EMU convergence plan sees debt ratio rising.
newsitem.headline: German EMU convergence plan sees debt ratio rising.

text.p: Germany's convergence plan for economic and monetary union (EMU) sees its debt ratio to Gross Domestic Product in 1997 rising to 61.5 percent, up from 60.7 percent in 1996, an EU source said on Friday.
Germany EMU convergence plans sees debt ratio rising

The convergence plan, which will be examined by EU finance ministers on Monday, includes economic estimates showing 2.5 percent GDP growth in 1997, a 1.5 percent rise in inflation and an assumption of a 6.2 percent yield on long-term government bonds.
The plan also envisages that unemployment in 1997 will not exceed an average of 4.1 million.
In January and February the number of those out of work was close to 4.8 million.
"It remains to be seen how far the Germans will have to undertake further (budget) efforts to keep in line with the numbers," the source said.
Bonn expects it 1997 deficit to average 2.9 percent of GDP which is based on the economic assumptions included in the convergence programme.
